title: fix: CCID layer has no recovery path for CCID-level errors from token (iccStatus, bError)
description:
The CCID spec (USB-CCID r1.10) defines two error fields in every RDR_to_PC_DataBlock response:
- iccStatus (bits 0-1 of bmICCStatus byte): 0=active, 1=inactive, 2=no ICC, 3=reserved
- bError: per-CCID error code when bmCommandStatus != 0

wp11_ccid.c validates CCID message type (0x80) and sequence number, but does not inspect bmICCStatus or bError in the response frame. If the reader returns a CCID error (e.g., token removed mid-operation, command aborted by reader), wolfP11 may mis-parse the response or misinterpret the payload as APDU data.

Fix:
1. After sequence number check (~line 320), read bmICCStatus from frame_in[7] (per CCID spec offset table)
2. If iccStatus == 1 or 2 (token inactive or absent), return WP11_CCID_ERR_NO_CARD (new error code) which maps to CKR_TOKEN_NOT_PRESENT in PKCS#11
3. Read bmCommandStatus from frame_in[7] bits 6-7: if non-zero (error or time extension), return WP11_CCID_ERR_USB unless it is a time extension request (bmCommandStatus==2), in which case wait and retry
4. Add comment citing CCID spec r1.10 Table 6.1.3 for the field offsets and meanings

This closes the gap between 'reader says error' and 'wolfP11 tries to parse the error response as a valid APDU'.
